## 1. Extraction: every numeral the block quotes (block lines 21-133)

Rule. block lines 21-133 read at the record pin; a numeral token is a maximal digit run with internal '.' or ',' groups (regex \d+(?:[.,]\d+)*|\.\d+) or a number word (zero..twelve, half; case-insensitive, word-bounded). Each token is classified in this order: inside a hand-mapped ledger row's span -> that row; inside a hand-declared exclusion span -> its category; else a generic rule (backticks, date, hash, arXiv/figure locator, file name or path, section sign, digits attached to a name, link/card/tier/stage/level/item/version prefix, one-/two-sided); else UNASSIGNED.

|---|---|

Ledger rows: 166 (hand-mapped, each a span of one block line). Hand exclusion spans: 31. Unassigned: **0**.

Numeral-free rows. Every numeral token above is assigned by the rule. A span without a numeral gets a row by this rule: a numeral-free span gets a row when the block lists it among the figures to be reproduced for the note: an entry of an item's figure list, a qualifier or definition attached to quoted figures, an N3(ii)-(v) result, or a figure label; requests for an account, a method, a provenance or a table get none (examples in numeral_free_no_row: Code's read of block lines 21-133, not an exhaustive enumeration). ## 2. The ledger

One row per figure as the block quotes it. 'item raw row' is the item raw's own line at the audit pin. 'printed', 'source' and 'status' are the item raw's, verbatim (long values are cut at 400 characters here; the JSON carries them whole). 'entry (record)' = the latest commit, over the row's record sources, at which a source entered the record (artifact: last change at or before the pin; line locator: the blamed commit); 'entry (+audit)' adds the audit raw (results/raw/2026-10-08_note-*) where the figure's only source is an audit raw (computed-new; source-only). A '(cont.)' line is a second primary item-raw row for the same figure; a '(see)' line carries N1's note on the row, the primary item-raw row's own note where the status cell does not already carry it (round 3; cut at 700 characters, whole in the JSON), and related item-raw rows, each with its own status (shown, not used in the pass check).

## 4. The block's pass check (block :23)

*N1 final:* 4a-4g are the provisional round's pass check over the block's quotations, kept as built. Where they say the note is not on this machine or defer to the --note run, section 9 is that run: 9d is the pass check over the note's own figures, 9e the watch-list per conditional STOP, and 9f the span notes that read the 4g corrections against the note's sentences.

*Pass:* every figure is `reproduced` or `log-only` with a locator. *On fail:* a `not found` figure is cut from the note; a `discrepant` figure is corrected in the note to the reproduced value if the discrepancy is transcription, and is a STOP on that item if it is not. ## 7. --note mode

Matching rule (round 2; the round-1 matcher compared values only and is replaced). Every numeral in each file (SVG: the text content of text, tspan, title and desc elements) is split into units: a fraction k/n is one unit; otherwise each numeral, with its sign (+, -, ±, or none; a dash after a letter, digit or bracket is a range or a hyphen, not a sign), its unit kind (percent; percentage points, written 'pp' or 'points'; a multiplier attached as '×' or 'x'; else a plain number) and its decimal places. A ledger row's units are those of its span; a numeral-free row takes the units of its primary item-raw rows' figure labels. A note unit is **matched** only if a row unit has the same unit kind, the same value, a compatible sign (none = +; zero is neutral) and the same integer/decimal form, AND the row's context words (its span and its item-raw figure labels) agree with the words of the note unit's own clause (round 3: bounded by ';', a table bar, a bullet or a sentence end) within 60 characters of the unit: one agreeing word that occurs in fewer than 5 rows' contexts, or two agreeing words of any kind (a lone stage, arm or map name such as 'SFT' or 'DPO' is not enough); the agreeing words are printed. A value hit without such agreement is a **candidate (verify context)**, printed with the row's span and status. When more than one row carries the value, a match is labelled **matched; value shared by N rows (verify which)** and every other row with the value is listed as a candidate (round 3). A unit with no such value hit is **not in ledger**; it lists loose hits (the same digits or proportion with a different unit kind, sign or integer/decimal form: 0.3% against −0.3 or 0.003), rounding hits (half-up, two or more places) and item-raw figure rows carrying the value, as pointers only. Bare integers below 100 are 'weak' and never matched. Units caught by the generic rules (dates, hashes, paths, identifiers, section signs) are listed as excluded. 'Matched' is a pointer for the reader, not a verification: the context test is a word overlap.

Limits. An SVG's plotted positions (point coordinates, bar heights) are geometry, not text, and are not read: F2's plotted (FPR, TPR) points must be checked against their data file (results/raw/2026-10-08_note-N2-roc.json for ours; N2vi for the source's) by a human or by the Draftsman seat's own export.

Watch-list. Every unit whose value is one of these is surfaced in its own table, whatever it matches (sign ignored; a decimal key with stated places matches only that many places). Each entry's quotes are asserted to occur in the item-raw line cited.

### 9g. The commit at which the last of the note's figures entered the record (the tag commit)

Rule, per figure (not-found figures enter nothing): a figure mapped to a ledger row takes that row's entry from sections 2-5; a figure mapped to record lines takes, per record locator, the latest blamed commit of its lines, and over its locators the earliest (a fact enters with its first carrier); a figure mapped to an item-raw figure row takes that row's record sources; a computed-new figure (by its own status, its ledger row's or its item-raw row's; or, where no record entry is found, by the row's source value or the item-raw line it cites) enters with the audit raw: the blamed commit of the first audit-raw line it cites; and a figure whose only carrier is an audit raw committed after the audit pin enters with that raw. Over figures, the latest. Each figure's entry and how it was found are in the JSON (`note_rows_final.entries`).

### 9i. Corrections recorded separately from status (round 5)

A correction is what the note's sentence should say, recorded beside the row's carried status, never as a status (the v0.3 final ledger's 10b). 'whose' says whether the reading is an item raw's or N1's own. Kind: wording, precision or scope. Since round 6 the script declares every correction, with its kind and whose reading it is (NR_CORRECTIONS, the v0.3 final ledger's 11b); the rows here are exactly those.

## 10. Values check: mutation self-test, overwrite guard, known limits (this run), and the round's record

Each mutation changes the rows data in memory and the validation runs again; it is caught when a failure no named exemption explains is reported, or when the run stops (a frozen hash, coverage, or an assertion on a row the script names). A mutation that is not caught, a control that is caught, or a known limit that is caught, stops the run before anything is written. The families are generated from the rows at every run. ### 10d. What the validator still does not catch

- Integer and word units can still pass at level B on another distinctive value the row states that is on a cited line (57 rows at level B). An integer unit's own number must be stated in the source_value (the unit-stated check), but the cited line need not carry it. The source-values check covers every decimal (one place or more) and every fraction a source_value states; an integer elsewhere in a source_value, neither the unit nor in a fraction, is not checked (self-test L03).
- A word unit ('one', 'two') passes at level A when the word occurs on a cited line, whatever its source_value says (self-test L02); the word can be a coincidence. S7#12 and S7#15 carry a locator-value exemption that says what their lines do carry.
- Status binding. The status check binds a row's status to the cited item-raw lines that give a status and carry a value the row states, to its quoted status_basis (an item-raw line; a single-term clause where its line gives several terms), or to the ledger row it names, which the ledger-bind check ties to the row. The row checks cannot tell a row's own figure line from another figure's line that carries the same value, or the clause that applies from another clause of the same line. So a status changed together with one more field can still pass them: a locator prefix with a reproduced figure row that carries one of the row's values (98 of the 301 rows whose status is computed-new, discrepant, not found or log-only; family G), a ledger_row swap to a row the locator binds (6 of 301; family H), a status_basis moved with the status to another line or clause of a cited item raw (L01, L04), and a 'related row' field cut to its ledger row (L05). Every such change also changes the input of the status freeze (NR_STATUS_SHA256), so the run fails (status-hash) unless the script is changed with it, where it shows in a diff. The freeze does not judge whether a status is right.
- The frozen declarations (NR_KIND_SHA256, NR_CLAUSE_SHA256, NR_STATUS_SHA256, NR_TEXT_SHA256, NR_EXEMPT_FP, NR_CORRECTIONS with its fingerprints, NR_QUOTE_REVIEWED, NR_DISC, the watch rows and the open items' rows) freeze; they do not judge. A row edited together with its declaration passes, and both show in a diff. Whether a unit is a figure, whether a clause is a fair cut of its sentence, and whether a status, a correction or a comment is right stays the mappers' and their checkers' reading.
- Ledger rows (rewritten in round 7). The ledger-span check accepts any named ledger row that carries the value, so a common value (0.000, 0.5) can pass on a wrong row. Since round 7 the ledger-bind check requires the row's first ledger id to be named in its locator, or one of that ledger row's item-raw lines to be cited, and every ledger id the locator names to be in ledger_row; a swap to a ledger row the locator binds passes the row checks (bullet 3). Every ledger_row change, of any status, fails the status freeze.
- Free text is frozen, not judged. NR_TEXT_SHA256 covers every comment, cause, not-figure reason and validation note, every change record (round5, round6, round7, round 8's n1v4_round2 and round8, and round 9's round9 and n1v5_round2, their 'why' and 'previous' included), the provenance fields n1v4_chain, v0_3_row, n1v5_chain and v0_4_row, the round-9 fields (scope_corrected_in_note, discharged, admitted_citation), every span note and annotation, and the file's how_built, schema and provenance; NR_CORRECTIONS' fingerprints cover each correction's text and basis. Beyond that, only the quotes the script asserts (NR_DISC's causes, the open items' and the watch-list's span notes, the round-9 fields' quotes) and the quotation scan read it.
- Not-found rows (round 7). A not-found row's locator and source value are in the status freeze, and every file and line they cite must exist (pins); whether the search they describe was complete stays the mappers' reading.
- The quotation scan (round 7) is a heuristic: a quoted span of fifteen words or more within reach of a name in NR_QUOTE_EXT_RE, in the rows file only. A long quotation without quotation marks, or with no such name nearby, is not flagged, and the script's own prose and the rendered ledger are not scanned; the rule on external quotations stays the author's to keep.
- Every check is a consistency check on the mapping; none re-derives a figure.
- Ruled corrections (round 8). NR_RULED_CORRECTIONS declares, per row, the PI's ruling (R1 of 2026-10-09), its condition line and quote, the figure row, the record's discrepant value and the corrected value; nr_check_ruled verifies the row against that declaration and the cited lines (X01-X09, X11-X13, X17, X22-X24, X34-X38, X52-X59, X63-X67; re-keyed in round 9 where the row is cut, 10a): the source's own clause (declared per row, 'source v1 text 0.000') stating exactly the ruled 0, verbatim on the figure row's line and in the row's source_value outside its bracketed note (fix round 3: a bare 0 elsewhere, '0 hits', '(0 places)', 'layer 0', no longer meets it; X11-X13), matched as a whole clause (fix round 4: no digit or decimal appended or prepended, so 'source v1 text 0.0009' or a declared 'source v1 text 0.0' does not meet it; X17; fix round 5: nor a comma and a digit, 'source v1 text 0.000,3', X24; fix round 6, Code's E4 (a): a whitelist, not a list of refused suffixes, X34-X38; fix round 7, Code's F3 and F4: every occurrence of the clause outside a bracketed note must be bound, not one, so a range restated beside the clause fails, X55; an occurrence has no word character, '.', format or combining character just before it, and is followed by the end of its field (a table cell of the figure row's line, the source_value) or by one of the declared terminators ' [', '; ', ', ' or ' (' each followed by a letter (by Unicode category, so not a superscript digit; since fix round 8, Code's G2, an ASCII letter, so not a modifier or other letter that looks like punctuation, ', ʹ0.003' or ', ª0.003', X66, X67), or ')' where a '(' opened outside a bracketed note before the clause in the field (fix round 8: the '(' counted outside notes, X65) and followed by the end of its field, a declared terminator or an ASCII letter (fix round 8: '(source v1 text 0.000)–0.003' and '(source v1 text 0.000)0.003' fail, X63, X64; NR_CLAUSE_END_RX, nr_clause_end_ok, nr_paren_close_ok), so a range or list ('0.000–0.003', '0.000-0.003', '0.000/0.003', '0.000 to 0.003', '0.000, 3', '0.000, .003', '0.000, −0.003', '0.000, ' with a zero-width space and a digit, '0.000)0.003', '0.000; 0.003', '0.000 (0.003)', '0.000, ³', and since fix round 8 '(0.000)–0.003', '(0.000)0.003', '(0.000) 0.003', '(0.000))', a ')' whose '(' is inside a note, ', ʹ0.003' and ', ª0.003') fails; X34-X38, X52-X59, X63-X67; what follows a declared terminator is not read past the letter after ', ', '; ', ' (' or ')', or past a bracketed note, so ' (to 0.003)', '; or 0.003', ', or 0.003', ', x0.003', ' [x] 0.003' or '(0.000)and' after the clause pass (Code's probes of fix rounds 7 and 8, 10e); nor is what precedes an occurrence read past the character before it, so a value before the clause passes ('0.003, source v1 text 0.000', '0.003–source v1 text 0.000', 'not source v1 text 0.000'; Code's probe of fix round 8, 10e): the figure row's line and every R1 row's source_value put the record's 0.003 before the clause by construction ('record A 0.003 / record B 0.003; source v1 text 0.000'), so the prefix side cannot be closed by a rule on what precedes the clause, and it is a declared limit: the whitelist binds the clause's end, not the rest of the field, and in the rows as built each R1 row's clause occurs once and ends at ' [' or at the end of its field), outside every bracketed note (fix round 5: a nested note is part of the note it sits in, and an unclosed '[' is read as a note running to the end of the field, so a clause inside a nested or unclosed note does not meet it; X22, X23; fix round 6: nr_bracket_mask), the ruled 0 in the condition's quote, and level A, which at zero places the record's 0.003 can meet on its own (X08, X09). The ruling itself is the PI's, routed to Code and stated in this script: no committed file carries it, so the script freezes it (a change shows in a diff) and does not judge it.
- Row tags (round 8 fix round, extended in fix rounds 3-8). A row tag on a line of an audit-outcome raw binds only in the strict form 'path@rev:n (Sx#n)' (the line's first table cell is that key; X10). Since fix round 6 (Code's E4 (b)) the rule is a whitelist, and since fix round 7 (Code's F3) it binds through the locator parser: in each of the five fields pins reads (locator, source_value, status_basis's and corrected_in_note's locators, and the correction's basis) that cites an audit-outcome raw, every character is printable ASCII, 0x20-0x7E (fix round 7: ASCII, so a format, combining, look-alike or full-width character fails the field; fix round 8, Code's G2: printable, so a control character such as DEL inside a key fails it too, X60), the escapes of '#' ('\#', '&#', '&num;') are refused (fix round 8, X61, X62), and a row key (S, digits, '#', ':' or '/', digits, in any case or spacing, inside any bracket or none; NR_ROW_KEY_ANY_RX) may appear only as ' (Sx#n)' directly after an NR_LOC_RE match that is a full 'path@rev:n' of an audit-outcome raw with one line number, the key that line's row; a tag after a bare revision, an item abbreviation, a bare continuation, a range or list, or on a path that is not an audit-outcome raw fails (X14, X15, X18, X47, X48), and so does every other occurrence of a key, after a line number or in prose. Not read as a key: one written with another separator ('S3-36', 'S3.36', 'S3 36'), a key in a field that cites no audit-outcome raw, the history records' 'previous' values (forms tested in Code's probe of fix round 7, 10e), and the free-text fields, which pins does not read (comment, cause, not-figure reason, validation note; frozen by NR_TEXT_SHA256): such a field can cite an audit-outcome raw and carry non-ASCII characters (S1#236's comment cites results/raw/2026-10-09_note-N1-v0_4-claims-ledger.md@fd2b136:1602-1609), and a key added to it is caught by the text freeze only. Fix round 6's strict-tag regex read the path differently from the parser, so a tag after '-@rev:n' or on a record path passed it (the round-6 script checker's forms, now X47, X48). Fix rounds 3-5 had refused loose forms one by one; each is still tested: a bare continuation and a range (X14, X15), a comma list, no space and an en-dash range (X18-X20), a bracket, other text in the parenthesis, 'row Sx#n', lower case, a space before '#', an em-dash range, a second tag after a strict one, a comma before the parenthesis and a slash list (X25-X33), and, added in fix round 6, a period, a spaced en dash, a spaced hyphen, a word, 'row', braces and full-width parentheses before or around the key (X39-X45) and a key in prose (X46), and, added in fix round 7, the bare-revision form, a strict-form tag on a record path, a key split by a zero-width space, a Cyrillic 'Ѕ' and a colon for '#' (X47-X51), and, added in fix round 8, DEL inside a key, a Markdown-escaped key in strict-tag position and an HTML-escaped key (X60-X62). In the rows as built for v0.5, no row key appears in a field pins reads: the rows that cite an audit-outcome raw (S1#236 and S1#237 on N1's v0.4 ledger at fd2b136, S3#129 on the v0.3 final ledger at ef5c446) carry no tag, so the tag mutations are re-keyed onto S1#236's and S1#237's locators (10a).
- History records (round 8 fix round, extended in fix round 3 and in round 9). The history-schema check (every change entry names its field and its previous value; no field changed twice from one previous value) runs in the final run and in the dev report alike, over every history field the profile freezes (v0_5: n1v4_round2, round8, round9 and n1v5_round2; NR_HISTORY_FIELDS), and mutations (X16 on a round9 record, X16b on a round8 record) assert that it fires at run level. It checks the records' form, not that a 'previous' equals the value it replaced; some 'previous' values carry a marker by declaration in place of a withdrawn clause (v0.4's, as its how_built states; round 9's integration edits on S1#260, S1#236 and S1#237 and its fix round 1's on S11#22, S1#390 and S1#112, how_built (4); in place, S11#22's and S11#23's round9 'why'), each marker replacing the withdrawn figure or clause only. Since fix round 1 every row that keeps a v0.4 key carries a round9 entry, with the v0.4 value as previous (null: absent), for each field that differs from its v0.4 row (note_file, note_line and the history and provenance fields apart); that is done when the rows file is built, and this script does not check it.
- Span-note cross-check (round 8 fix round 3, extended in fix round 4). The v0_4 profile requires the table (NR_REQUIRE_SPAN_DISPOSITION): a run whose table is absent, or misses a span note, stops at the profile gate, and the cross-check also runs in the validation stage ('span-note-crosscheck'; X21 appends a span note in memory and the self-test asserts the check fires); a 'carried' note must name an item that is not CLOSED. The table's dispositions are Code's declarations; the check binds their form and their cross-references, not whether a note's finding is in substance discharged.
- Ruling 6 (round 9; the PI's ruling 6 of 2026-10-10). nr_check_scope_corrected reads the item raw's correction from the cited line (the quote from its marker to the end of its sentence or cell) and the note's text that applies it (the note_quote, verbatim on the note line; on a render, on the row's node and the next nodes, newline-joined, up to six, the quote starting in the row's own node, _r9_svg_join), and binds them lexically: every number, layer label, relation and content word of the applied alternative inside the unit's own clause span, which stops at a later clause stating a figure of its own; and the discrepant claim (the replaced text, the figure's relation, its qualifier) carried neither in the note_quote nor in the unit's sentence on the note line (RP1-RP4, RP7-RP15, RP18-RP23, RP29-RP31; RP19, retargeted at fix round 1, patches the line past the row's note_quote, so it reaches the unit's-sentence branch; RP31 keeps a consistent note_quote across a render's joined nodes while the scope changes). The reading is Code's and lexical: a rewording that keeps the correction's words while changing its sense, or a scope stated outside the unit's sentence, is not read; the chains' span notes and checkers read each one against the note. Whether ruling 6 reaches a render's correction is the PI's to confirm, so F1a's two TS rows are reported open, not passing (ts_note_spans).
- Ruling 7 (round 9). nr_check_discharged binds each discharged row to ruling 7's table: the declared clause verbatim on the row's note line, W8's ledger row and item raw, the clause stating the overall rate and the per-arm range, and neither discrepant wording on the whole line, each read as a class of wordings (Code's lexical set, NR_ROUND9['w8']['absent']: uniformity over the arms, and a single ~1% rate per arm; RP5, RP16, RP24-RP27). A discrepant wording outside that set is a known limit, not a pass the ruling makes.
- Ruling 8 (round 9). nr_check_admitted binds an admitted citation to ruling 8's table: a (note line, unit) the PI names (NR_ROUND9['r8_units']), the declared cited source and note text verbatim on a line of the note, the row a 'not found' figure mapped to none; a run-level check requires each admitted unit to occur on its line at least as often as the file's rows claim it there (RP6, RP17, RP28). It does not read whether the cited source says what the note attributes to it; the citations are the PI's admission, not record figures.
- Ruling 5 (round 9). nr_r9_committed passes a computed-new row when every audit raw it cites is committed: its revision an ancestor of HEAD at the run, the file in that commit's tree, every cited line present (R5-01 to R5-06). It does not read whether the audit raw's line computes the figure (the row checks do), and it reads HEAD's ancestry, so it holds for a tag commit that descends from HEAD. A computed-new row whose pass rests on a routed reading or a condition not met as written is declared in NR_ROUND9['cn_held'] and reported open, not passing (9d); the table is Code's reading of which rows wait, a run-level check binds it to computed-new figure rows of the file, each with a reason, its declared locus (file, line and unit) asserted against the row, and a 9h item whose rows include it (RP32-RP35; since fix round 2); it does not read the item's text, and no check finds a row that should be held and is not.
- Fields outside the schema and the freezes (round 9 fix round 1, script checker finding 5). A row field or a top-level key of the rows file that no check reads and no freeze covers is inert: it changes no check, no status and no pass, and nothing reports it (the self-test's own '_r9_touch' marker relies on that). The schema's fields are listed in the rows file ('schema').
